newsitem.title: USA: Kansas to ask for year extention in property case.
newsitem.headline: Kansas to ask for year extention in property case.

text.p: The Kansas Attorney General's Office plans to ask a district court judge for a one-year extension to get about 21 of the state's 105 counties in compliance with property appraisal guidelines, according to a deputy attorney general.

John Campbell, senior deputy attorney general, said the office may file a motion as early as next week in Shawnee County District Court asking for more time to allow the remaining counties to catch up with the rest of the state.

The motion comes in a 1992 lawsuit filed by the Kansas attorney general against various state officials, including the property evaluation director, who has supervisory responsibility for appraisals. The lawsuit charged that 99 of the counties at that time were not complying with the state's property tax appraisal system.

Campbell said that in many cases appraisals of residential, commercial and agricultural properties in counties were too low, causing inequities in a 35-mill state-wide property tax the state was collecting to equalize per-pupil funding of public schools.
Since 1992, appraisal compliance has been achieved in most of the 99 counties, with an estimated 21 counties not in compliance, Campbell said.
